kai-mgr: Quick ask  we're prepping a promotion packet and hit a question in the leveling rubric: does owning cross-team operational SLAs count as a scope increase or just execution excellence? Trying to pick the right "why" wording.

maria-hr: Good Q. Owning cross-team SLAs is scope increase if it expands decision authority (owning vendor contracts, setting SLAs, approving infra spend) or influences hiring/roadmap. If it's execution-only (runs runbooks but no decision authority) highlight sustained ownership but frame as impact not scope.

jamal-comp: To add: committee looks for trajectory. If the role now has regular cross-functional negotiation or budget sign-off, treat as a level change. Provide examples: "negotiated X vendor terms" or "approved Y tradeoffs" to show authority.

kai-mgr: Makes sense. Is there a preferred phrasing for "impact" bullets? I'm worried being too fluffy.

elaine-peopleops: Use metrics + frequency. Tiny template: "What I did" (1 line), "Why it mattered" (metric or stakeholder quote), "How often / since when" (start date). Example: "Led incident runbook ownership (since 2028-11), reduced P1 escalation by 40% and cut mean time to recovery from 4h to 1.5h."

kai-mgr: Helpful. Another practical: how many peer calibration notes should we include for a standard packet?

maria-hr: Typically 2-3 anonymized peer calibration bullets. For borderline packets include an extra peer from a related func to show cross-team view.

jamal-comp: And call out internal parity explicitly: pick 2 peers at the target level and say how the candidate compares on scope & outcomes. That speeds the committee.

calibration-bot: FYI calibration slot availability: next peer calibration session 1912346800 UTC. If you drop materials 24h before, we'll schedule a 15m slot.

kai-mgr: Good to know. One more: if we want comp at midpoint +8% but the manager wants exact $ amount in the packet, any preference?

maria-hr: We prefer band/percentile (e.g., midpoint +8%). The committee evaluates against internal bands; exact $ makes parity harder to parse. If you include $ also include the band percentile.

jamal-comp: If requesting >10% bump without level change mark as "exceptional comp" and include retention risk evidence (counteroffers, criticality). Finance will ask for funding source in that case.

kai-mgr: What's the typical turnaround for a calibration note -> committee decision path?

elaine-peopleops: If packet is complete and not exceptional: 7 business days. If you need faster, mark "expedite" and note business reason; ad-hoc committee may be possible but requires exec champion.

payroll-bot: payroll_cutoff=1912347200 UTC for next payroll window. Submit approved packets by then to be eligible for retroactive pay to requested effective_date.

kai-mgr: Thanks all. I'll reword bullets with the metric template, attach two peer notes, and drop the packet 36h before the calibration session.

maria-hr: Ping us if you want a quick pre-check of wording  we can scan for weak verbs and add one-line suggestions.

kai-mgr: Appreciated. Will do.
